results.summary: The RGB Mixer demo takes inputs from three digital encoders, debounces them, and produces three PWM outputs whose duty cycles correspond to the encoder values. It is intended to be tested by twisting each encoder and observing the brightness of LEDs connected to the PWM outputs. For debugging, setting the debug port to 0, 1, or 2 outputs the internal encoder value on the bidirectional pins. The design requires three external digital encoders and was reported working by the author, who checked all three channels.

The Wave Generator produces sine, sawtooth, triangular, and square waveforms with selectable amplitude and phase parameters, outputting 8-bit two's complement fixed-point values in parallel or via a write-only SPI interface. It is configured by setting waveform selection pins and loading amplitude and phase values through a parameter bus, then enabling generation. An external SPI DAC is needed to convert the digital output to an analog signal. The design is notable for its flexible parameter control and the SPI interface that enables connection to a DAC, with a maximum sampling frequency of 1.65 MHz.

This design implements a USB Communications Device Class (CDC) device with two virtual serial ports, each providing a different application. It is based on the usb_cdc repository and requires a 1.5k pull-up resistor on D+ and a 48 MHz clock to enumerate as two serial ports on a host computer. External hardware includes a USB cable with exposed wires, a 1.5k resistor, and optionally buttons for inputs. A silicon tester confirmed it works, showing two serial ports and verifying that each input sent alternating capital and lowercase letters.

FazyRV-ExoTiny is a minimal System-on-Chip based on the FazyRV RISC-V core that uses external QSPI ROM and RAM for program storage and data memory. It converts Wishbone bus accesses into QSPI transfers, enabling continuous mode for the ROM to reduce latency, and supports Quad Mode for the RAM. The design requires external QSPI flash and RAM chips, such as the W25Q128JV and APS6404L-3SQR, and careful reset synchronization; its implementation is near the edge of timing convergence.

The Minibyte CPU is a simple 8-bit processor featuring a custom RISC instruction set, built-in design-for-test features, and an optional demo ROM for easy testing. It exposes debug output select lines, halt control, and a register enable, along with an 8-bit data bus and address/write-enable outputs. The design was created primarily as a learning and reference project to gain familiarity with Verilog. It requires some external hardware to run the demo ROM.

This co-processor reads data from four sensors sequentially and compares each reading to previous data to detect deviations, also identifying sensor faults and providing warning signals along with sensor identification. It is intended for precision farming applications and requires an external 8-bit ADC to convert sensor data. The design outputs a deviation detector signal, fault warnings, and sensor identifiers. The documentation is limited to a basic description and a single test example, without full implementation details.

This design implements a stepper motor controller using a Moore state machine with selectable speeds (1s, 0.5s, 0.25s, 0.125s), direction control, and three step types: full, half, and double. It is controlled by inputs for reset, select, direction, and step mode, and outputs four coil signals. External hardware includes an FPGA (Cyclone II EP2C35F672C6ES) for testing, and the design is documented in Spanish with simulation waveforms for various combinations. The project appears to be an educational exercise, providing a didactic implementation of stepper motor control.

This design implements a 10-bit moving average filter that smooths input data streams using registers and a finite state machine, with the filter width determined by the FILTER_POWER parameter. It processes digital input values presented on the ui_in port and produces smoothed outputs on uo_out, with control signals on uio_in to select filter width and operation. The design includes strobe input and output for data synchronization. Testing involves providing varying input patterns and filter widths to evaluate the filter's response.

This project is a simple 2-bit multiplier implemented using combinational logic gates, specifically AND gates and half adders made from AND and XOR gates. It takes two 2-bit inputs (a and b) and produces a 4-bit product output, with a full truth table provided in the documentation. External hardware required includes a 4-position DIP switch for inputs and 4 LEDs for outputs, both with appropriate resistors. The design is presented as a practical and didactic exercise to go from Verilog description to a physical circuit.

This power management IC generates two complementary PWM outputs with duty cycles controlled by an external ADC, using a heartbeat signal to periodically initiate ADC conversions and update the PWM. It reads an 8-bit parallel ADC (AD7819) and drives a high-side driver (MCP14700) for a half-bridge configuration, with a built-in dead zone to prevent shoot-through. The design uses state machines to sequence ADC read and PWM update, and is intended for power conversion applications. External hardware includes the specified ADC and high-side driver.
